description:
GO BEYOND is a team of two students passionate about space, science, and technology.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing SPACE LEGACY: The Forgotten Missions, a 3D browser-based simulator where users explore the Moon, discover abandoned scientific equipment, and learn about its history and purpose.

Our goal is to make space science interactive, educational, and accessible to everyone 

GO BEYOND — Think beyond Earth.
summary: SPACE LEGACY is a browser-based 3D educational experience created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It transforms the history of abandoned lunar equipment into an interactive learning journey. Users can explore a simulated lunar environment, discover historic Apollo-era equipment, and learn through a scientific archive, an educational lunar laser ranging simulation, quizzes, a field journal, and mission progress. Built with JavaScript and Three.js, the project makes the scientific and historical legacy of lunar exploration more accessible and engaging. The current prototype focuses on the Moon, with a future vision of expanding to Mars.
details:
PROJECT OVERVIEW

SPACE LEGACY is an interactive 3D educational project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge challenge "Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

The project addresses an important educational challenge: while famous space missions are widely remembered, the scientific equipment and experiments left behind on the Moon are less familiar to the public. These objects represent an important part of humanity's scientific and technological history.

OUR SOLUTION

SPACE LEGACY transforms lunar exploration history into an interactive browser-based experience. Users enter a simulated lunar environment from a first-person perspective and explore selected historical objects from Apollo-era missions.

The current prototype includes:

  • First-person lunar exploration.
  • Interactive scanning of selected objects.
  • A scientific archive with historical information.
  • An educational simulation explaining lunar laser ranging.
  • Interactive quizzes.
  • A digital field journal.
  • Mission progress features.

The experience includes educational content about the Apollo 11 lunar laser ranging retroreflector, Apollo surface experiments, the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), and the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION AND NASA RESOURCES

Official NASA historical resources are used to inform the project's descriptions and educational context. These include NASA materials about the Apollo 11 Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package (EASEP), lunar laser ranging retroreflectors, the Apollo 14 ALSEP station, and the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle.

The lunar terrain in the current prototype is procedurally generated. The project does not claim to integrate a live NASA data feed or a NASA lunar terrain dataset. NASA resources serve as historical and scientific references for the educational content.

TECHNOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENT

The project was developed using:

  • JavaScript for interactive functionality.
  • Three.js for browser-based 3D visualization.
  • Procedurally generated geometry and lunar terrain.
  • HTML and CSS for the web experience.
  • Netlify for public deployment.

CREATIVITY AND EDUCATIONAL IMPACT

The creative approach is to turn historical space equipment into an interactive storytelling experience. Instead of only reading about abandoned equipment, users can explore a simulated environment, discover selected objects, and learn why these artifacts matter.

SPACE LEGACY aims to make planetary exploration history more accessible, encourage scientific curiosity, and inspire students to learn about space exploration and engineering.

FUTURE VISION

The current version is a lunar prototype. With future funding, scientific review, and further development, SPACE LEGACY could grow into a broader digital planetary heritage and education platform.

Potential development includes:

  • A more detailed historical and scientific archive.
  • Educational environments about Mars missions and their equipment.
  • English, Russian, and Tajik language support.
  • More detailed 3D environments and simulations.
  • Learning materials for schools and teachers.
  • Improved accessibility across devices.

These are proposed future goals, not features currently completed.

TEAM

Abubakr — Team Leader, Project Creator & Lead Developer.

Sanjar — Team Assistant.

Our vision is to preserve the stories behind humanity's exploration equipment and make this scientific legacy accessible to a wider audience.
